newsitem.title: GERMANY: KAL Cargo merges Nordic sales with German.
newsitem.headline: KAL Cargo merges Nordic sales with German.

text.p: Korean Air Lines Co (KAL) said its German cargo division has taken over responsibility for freight sales in Scandinavia to try to improve its market share in the region.
Korean Air Cargo Germany has been responsible for all sales activities in Sweden, Norway, Denmark and Finland since May 1, 1997, a statement said.
General sales agents in Scandinavia would continue to sell the airline's cargo space but under the supervision and with the support of Germany-based staff, it added.
Korean Air Cargo said it has integrated its Germany and Scandinavia budgets into a single budget and named German staff to oversee Scandinavia market development.
German sales manager Robert M. Instinsky was now also sales manager for Scandinavia and would personally oversee the Swedish and Finland markets.
Northern Germany regional sales manager Klaus Ehlers was now responsible for Norway and Denmark, while eastern Germany sales manager Christine Burger would also support the Danish market.

Scandinavian freight would be integrated into the airline's new European trucking network with connections to 16 weekly flights between Frankfurt and Seoul and 34 Asia/Pacific trans-shipment destinations.
"Thanks to these measures, Korean Air is now in a position to cover the large potential of the Nordic countries comprehensively and to seize significant market shares," the statement said.
Korean Air Cargo Germany increased revenue over the first four months of 1997 by 6.5 percent with traffic to Korea and Australia/New Zealand contributing in particular to the growth, it added.
